```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dpi = 150,
  out.width = "100%", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
```

ggjbrowse reads a region of a BAM, CRAM, GFF3, BED, BigBed, BigWig, VCF or
pairwise alignment file through the [JBrowse 2](https://jbrowse.org) genome
browser's own data engine, run in V8. A reader returns the tables the
browser's display draws from, and `autoplot()` draws them as the browser's
track.

- Every example below runs on clips of public data installed with the
  package.
- `locus` is written as JBrowse's location box writes it, 1-based.
- `width` is the view's width in pixels: a reader lays out labels, rows and
  zoom levels as a JBrowse view that wide does.

```{r setup}
library(ggjbrowse)
library(ggplot2)

e <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "ggjbrowse")
locus <- "chr12:6,534,201-6,538,700"
width <- 900
```

## A track in one call

We'll start with nanopore direct RNA reads across _GAPDH_ from NA12878.
`autoplot()` draws the browser's alignments track: junction arcs over the
coverage, and the reads split at each intron.

```{r reads}
reads <- jbrowse_alignments(e("gapdh_direct_rna.bam"), locus, width = width)
p <- autoplot(reads)
```

```{r reads-plot, fig.width = jbrowse_width(p), fig.height = jbrowse_height(p)}
p
```

## The tables

The result is a list of data frames, one per kind of mark the display draws.
Each read has its pileup `row` and the `color` the display paints it, and
each mismatch, gap and clip names its read by a key.

```{r tables}
names(reads)
head(reads$reads[c("chrom", "start", "end", "row", "strand", "mapq",
  "color")])
```

The geoms draw one table each, so a figure is an ordinary ggplot that `+`
changes piece by piece. Here the reads are filled by mapping quality:

```{r mapq, fig.height = 3}
ggplot(reads) +
  geom_jbrowse_reads(aes(fill = mapq)) +
  geom_jbrowse_mismatches() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  scale_y_reverse()
```

## The display's settings and decisions

A reader's `display` argument takes the track's display settings, spelled as
a JBrowse config writes them, so a setting copied from a config or a session
draws the same in R:

```{r strand}
stranded <- jbrowse_alignments(e("gapdh_direct_rna.bam"), locus,
  width = width,
  display = list(encoding = list(color = list(field = "strand"))))
```

What the display decided comes back as columns. `shown` marks the junctions
it draws, so setting it keeps only the junctions with 60 reads or more:

```{r junctions}
reads$junctions$shown <- reads$junctions$count >= 60
p <- autoplot(reads)
```

```{r junctions-plot, fig.width = jbrowse_width(p), fig.height = jbrowse_height(p)}
p
```

## Several tracks

`jbrowse_stack()` stacks tracks as a JBrowse view does, top to bottom on one
x axis, each named for its track, with the keys collected:

```{r stack}
genes <- jbrowse_features(e("gapdh_gencode.gff3.gz"), locus, width = width)
phylop <- jbrowse_wiggle(e("gapdh_phylop100way.bw"), locus, width = width)
fig <- jbrowse_stack(GENCODE = genes, phyloP = phylop, Reads = stranded)
```

```{r stack-plot, fig.width = jbrowse_width(fig), fig.height = jbrowse_height(fig)}
fig
```

- `jbrowse_height()` and `jbrowse_width()` give the size that keeps the
  display's pixel proportions:
  `ggsave("gapdh.png", fig, width = jbrowse_width(fig), height = jbrowse_height(fig))`.
- Each band is a ggplot, so `fig & theme_classic()` restyles every band, and
  `+` reaches only the last.
- Several loci lay out end to end, as a view lays out several regions: give
  a reader `c("chr12:6,534,201-6,535,700", "chr12:6,537,201-6,538,700")`.

## Genotypes

`jbrowse_variants()` reads a multi-sample VCF as the variant matrix: a row
per sample, a column per record. A sample table adds columns to the rows, so
the display can color them, here 100 people of the 1000 Genomes Project at
_DCST2_ by superpopulation:

```{r variants, fig.height = 5}
v <- jbrowse_variants(e("1000g_dcst2.vcf.gz"), "1:155,000,001-155,050,000",
  samples = e("1000g_dcst2_samples.tsv"),
  display = list(rowColor = list(field = "superpopulation")))
autoplot(v, layout = "columns")
```

`as.matrix(v)` gives the genotypes as a sample-by-record matrix, and a tree
set as `v$tree <- hclust(dist(as.matrix(v)), "average")` orders the rows and
draws beside them.

## Two genomes

`jbrowse_synteny()` reads a PAF, chain or delta file between two regions as
the synteny view's ribbons. HG002's maternal chr8 over its paternal copy shows
the 4 Mb inversion at 8p23.1 as a crossing ribbon:

```{r synteny, fig.height = 3}
r <- "5,250,001-14,250,000"
autoplot(jbrowse_synteny(e("hg002_chr8.chain"), paste0("chr8_MATERNAL:", r),
  paste0("chr8_PATERNAL:", r),
  display = list(encoding = list(color = list(field = "strand"))),
  swap = TRUE, labels = c(query = "paternal", target = "maternal")))
```

`jbrowse_dotplot()` reads the same files as a dotplot, and
`jbrowse_multiway()` lays several genomes in lanes.

## From a JBrowse view

The linear genome view's **Export R script** menu item, from JBrowse
5.0.0-beta.14, writes a script of this shape for the view on screen: one reader per open track, at the view's
regions, width and display settings, then `jbrowse_stack()` and `ggsave()`.
